question: Does detcore's per-thread LOCAL virtual clock get bumped FORWARD to the GLOBAL (committed) time at every thread<->scheduler interaction, as the time-model's designer states the invariant? Measure the actual global-minus-local gap distribution; determine where the invariant holds and where it does not; check whether any recent time-policy change (#1095/#1190/vtime-jump/--no-rcb-time) blunted or froze virtual time.
kind: research/audit only -- NO source changes (virtual time is SACRED)

repos.note: prior source-level audit ai_docs/detcore-global-vs-local-vtime-audit_20260801.md ground SHA hermit 09207d80; this run re-verifies at 4274144d and adds empirical + unit-test evidence the earlier audit could not run (compile break fixed by 36ee7e70).

instrumentation: RUST_LOG=detcore=trace; NO source modification. GLOBAL from 'advancing committed_time from X to Y' / '[sched-step3] ... committed_time C' lines; LOCAL from '[dtid N] updated rcb clock, new logical time' lines.
method: parse_gap.py pairs each per-dtid LOCAL sample with the most recent GLOBAL committed_time; gap = global - local; reports min/med/p90/p99/max per dtid and pooled (ALL).

git_blame.observe_guest_clock max-floor: c4a4bba2 2026-07-28 detcore: normalize guest clock after exec (#1190)
git_blame.use_thread_local_clock_reads: a520b67c 2026-07-27 PR #845 Improve SaBRe exec and inherited descriptor compatibility

findings_summary.invariant_literal_bump_local_to_global_T: FALSE (by design) -- local clock never rises to GlobalTime total; gap = Sigma(other threads) + extra_time never collapses at interactions.
findings_summary.real_forward_bump_exists: TRUE -- send_and_update_time advance_to(lower_bound); but target is per-thread lower bound (own-slice threads_time), not the global total.
findings_summary.per_turn_global_advance_floor: exact 500000 ns = NANOS_PER_SCHED (measured; median per-turn ~604020 ns).
findings_summary.guest_visible_clock_reflects_global_mono: TRUE -- default use_thread_local_clock_reads=false -> reads global lower bound -> observe_guest_clock max-floor pins monotonic across the shared Arc process tree.
findings_summary.fake_determinism_check: PASS -- guest-observed times NOT round/blunted (first read 1767225600.233056510, not .000000000); no exact-integer-second values; first post-exec read carries committed time forward (refutes #1095 origin-reset).
findings_summary.recent_changes_weakened_continuity: NO -- #1190 max-floor supersedes #1095 reset; unit tests green; values un-blunted; the structural global>local gap predates all suspects.
